summary: One-off script that restates every money value in the Yard database in US dollars (millions), keeps the original reported figure beside it, and fills some empty budget fields from already-cited sources.
purpose: Makes budgets comparable across projects that were recorded in other currencies or in raw dollars, while keeping a record of what the source actually said.
why: The header says the change was requested by the owner after a sanity audit. The conversion rules are explained in the header comment.
how: It opens one database transaction, reads all projects and active evidence quotes, and works out for each budget field whether the reported figure is in another currency. It converts when the rate year is clear and refuses when the figure is a range, bound, or ambiguous. It records each change in the change log and writes a JSON report. Without the commit flag the transaction is rolled back.
inputs: The projects table, the evidence_quotes table, and the DATABASE_URL setting. The --commit flag switches from dry run to real writes.
outputs: A JSON report under data/repairs (dry-run or commit file), new rows in change_log, and updated attributes and budget columns when committed.
risks: Writes to live budget columns. A bad rate or a misread currency would change figures the owner relies on. Only the planned and actual budget figures for projects are touched.
debug: Open the newest report under data/repairs and read the refused and currencyRelabelled lists. Compare a refused project's stored value with its quote. Re-run without --commit to see the plan first.
